I'm 63 years old, been farming these 20 mu in Quzhou since I was ten. My father taught me everything, and now my son and his wife both work over at the factory in Handan, so it's mostly me and my wife on the land. I only finished primary school, but I know my fields better than any book. I don't need an extension agent to tell me when the soil is ready.

I split my 20 mu into two parts: 10 mu for cotton and 10 mu for wheat-maize double cropping. I've done it this way for twenty years. Cotton brings the most money when prices are decent, but wheat and maize are my insurance. If the bollworms hit the cotton or the price drops, I still have grain to sell and flour for the family. Diversification is how I sleep at night.

**The wheat** went in last October, same as always. I plowed the field in autumn and put down base fertilizer before planting — about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. You can't skip that. In March when the wheat greened up, I topdressed with about 20 kg of urea per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang only used 15 kg, but I think 20 kg is safer. Last year I used 18 kg and the plants looked a bit yellow, so this year I added a little more. I already irrigated once at green-up, and I'll irrigate one more time at jointing if the rain doesn't come. Two irrigations for wheat, that's what I've always done. I spray herbicide once in spring, and if I see aphids I'll spray for them too. I hire the combine for harvest in early June — costs about 50 yuan per mu but it's fast. I expect about 400 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather holds.

**The maize** goes in right after wheat harvest, mid-June. The window is tight — maybe five to seven days, no more. If I'm slow, the yield drops. I usually plant with the machine if I can get it; otherwise me and my brother do it by hand. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about 25 kg per mu. If the plants look yellow at the big喇叭口 stage, I might topdress with another 10-15 kg of urea, but I'll decide when I see them. Maize doesn't need much spraying — just herbicide once. For water, I irrigate once in July if it's dry, maybe twice if August is hot. The pumping costs money so I watch it. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

**The cotton** is my main crop and takes the most work. I plant in late April when the soil warms up. I buy hybrid seed, about 1.5 kg per mu, costs me 35 yuan per mu. I don't save cotton seed — the hybrid loses vigor. I plow and harrow the 10 mu, then put base fertilizer down before planting: about 30 kg compound fertilizer per mu plus 5 kg urea. When the cotton starts budding in July, I topdress with another 15 kg urea per mu. I irrigate twice for sure — once after planting if it don't rain, and once at flowering. Maybe a third time if August is real dry, but electricity for the well pump adds up. I spray for weeds right after planting, and I watch for aphids and bollworms all summer. That's my biggest worry. Me and my wife can pick some, but 10 mu is too much for just us. I hire women from the village for picking — pay them by the day or by the kilo. That's my biggest labor cost, but there's no way around it. I hope to get 240 kg of lint per mu if the weather cooperates.

Money is always tight. My son sends some money back from the city, which helps, but I still can't afford to throw inputs around like those big business farms with 200 mu. I do what I did last year unless something big changes. Last year was okay — not great, not terrible — so I'm keeping things about the same. I'd rather spend a little too much on fertilizer than too little and risk a bad year. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, that's what I've learned in 53 years.
